stem: The 2-year spot rate is 4.0% and the 3-year spot rate is 4.6%, both with annual compounding. The implied 1-year forward rate two years from now (2y1y) is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 4.30% is the simple average of the two spot rates, not the marginal forward rate.
rationale.B: Correct. No arbitrage requires 1.046^3 = 1.04^2 × (1 + f), giving f = 5.81%.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 4.60% is the 3-year spot rate; on an upward-sloping curve the forward lies above the spot rate.

stem: The 1-year spot rate is 2.5% and the 1-year forward rate one year from now (1y1y) is 3.5%. The 2-year spot rate is closest to:

rationale.A: Correct. The 2-year spot rate is the geometric mean of the 1-year spot and the 1y1y forward.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 6.09% is the total 2-year return (1.025 × 1.035 − 1); it has not been annualised.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 3.50% is the forward rate; the spot rate is an average of the 2.5% and 3.5% rates.

stem: The 1-year and 2-year spot rates are 2.0% and 3.0% (annual compounding). The 2-year par rate is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 3.00% is the 2-year spot rate; on an upward-sloping curve the par rate is slightly lower.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 2.50% is the simple average of the spot rates, which is not how par rates are derived.
rationale.C: Correct. The coupon that prices a 2-year bond at par using the spot rates is 2.99%.

stem: An analyst argues that the government yield curve slopes upward even though investors expect short-term rates to remain unchanged, because investors require extra compensation for holding longer maturities. This view is most consistent with:
explanation: Liquidity preference theory says forward rates equal expected future spot rates plus a premium for bearing the risk of longer maturities, so the curve can slope upward with flat rate expectations.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Under unbiased expectations an upward slope must mean rates are expected to rise; there is no risk premium.
rationale.B: Correct. A liquidity (term) premium for longer maturities produces an upward slope even with unchanged expectations.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Segmented markets attributes rates to supply and demand within separate maturity segments, not to a premium for maturity risk.
